purpose: How an operator decides what a tax preparation practice may legally sign and file, which client segment and service model it commits to, how the season's arrival curve and the practice's peak capacity bound the work it can accept, and how a per-return fee is constructed from the return's real complexity drivers rather than from a refund outcome.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

the practice sells preparation and filing of tax returns for a fee charged per return to a client base that largely returns each year; the filing season, not the calendar month, is the operating period every decision is measured against

every requirement named in this knowledge base is an obligation CLASS, never a statement of current rule: preparer identification, credential and representation classes, electronic filing authorization, state and local registration, credit due-diligence duties and taxpayer-data protection duties all change between seasons and must be verified with the relevant authority in the practice's own jurisdiction before anything is planned around them

no fee, price band, return volume, capacity figure, cost item or break-even point in this knowledge base is a market rate or an industry benchmark; each is a mechanism the practice measures inside its own records and re-measures every season

the practice holds the densest identity and income package a household possesses, so confidentiality and least-privilege access discipline apply from the first marketing contact onward, not from the moment a return is opened
returns are prepared and signed only by people whose authorization class is known and current; work above that class is referred out rather than attempted
a first season must be planned on assumed shapes that will be wrong in their details, so every planning parameter here is treated as a hypothesis the season's own record will correct
exclusions: the per-return production pipeline - intake, document collection, preparation, review, signature and transmission - and the throughput controls that keep it accurate at peak: owned by the return workflow, accuracy and documentation knowledge base

error classes and their controls, the per-return due-diligence documentation habit and its retention workflow, the research-escalate-decline decision on an individual ambiguous item, and operational data handling inside a live return: owned by the same return workflow knowledge base

what makes clients return annually and how they are retained, post-season client follow-up and next-year positioning, referral growth, and the off-season revenue lines (the extension book as a service line, amendments, quarterly estimates, planning-adjacent education, bookkeeping crossover) together with capacity smoothing across the year: owned by the returning clients and off-season revenue knowledge base

tax advice, positions or conclusions on any specific taxpayer's facts; this knowledge base is practice-design and process knowledge only and is educational rather than personalized financial, legal or tax advice

any promise or implication about refund size or refund speed, any fee arrangement that varies with refund amount, any use of audit or penalty fear as a closing lever, and any sale that exploits a filer's urgency, distress, age or language barrier
invented fee tables, competitor price lists, market rates, volume benchmarks, industry margin figures or market-size claims presented as fact
representation before a tax authority beyond what the practice's credential class permits, legal opinions, attest and audit engagements, and bookkeeping or accounting instruction for clients

current statutory specifics - deadline dates, credit parameters, penalty amounts, mandate thresholds, renewal fees - which change between seasons and must be read from the authority's own current publications

competency_questions.question: What exactly does this practice sell, to whom, and what is the one unit that pricing, capacity and revenue are all counted in?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PRACTICE_CHARTER names the revenue unit as a completed, signed, accepted return, states the season as the operating period and lists what the practice will never sell; SEGMENT_COMMITMENT_DECISION names the client class it is sold to

competency_questions.question: Which preparer authorization and registration classes must be in place before I can accept a paid return, which of them govern representation rights, and which states am I actually allowed to prepare for?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CREDENTIAL_CLASS_MAP distinguishes the paid-preparer identification obligation, the unenrolled and limited-standing classes and the fully credentialed classes with their representation rights and renewal duties; STATE_REGISTRATION_LAYER produces a dated served-states list with the requirement class satisfied per state; both instruct that current rules be verified with the authority

competency_questions.question: What has to exist before I can transmit returns electronically, and how far ahead of the season must it be arranged?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EFILE_AUTHORIZATION_PATH describes the provider authorization as a long-lead application with a suitability review, names the firm-level ownership and update duties, the volume-based filing mandate class and the transmission-monitoring habit, and places the application in the off-season

competency_questions.question: Which returns will this practice accept, which will it refuse or refer, and how much credit due-diligence exposure is it willing to carry?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMPETENCE_PERIMETER gives accepted, conditional and referred-out return classes with the control that makes each conditional class acceptable; DUE_DILIGENCE_EXPOSURE_CLASS states the obligation class attached to certain credits and statuses and its consequences for time, price, training and exposure appetite

competency_questions.question: How do I market and sell preparation without promising a refund outcome, without selling on fear, and without taking advantage of a filer who cannot evaluate the work?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HONEST_OFFER_STANCE states refund-neutral selling, the ban on fear-driven urgency, the vulnerable-filer care rule and position neutrality as refusal-backed standing rules rather than tone

competency_questions.question: What must be true about how client data is held and who can reach it before the first document arrives?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SECURITY_INFRASTRUCTURE_PREREQ names the obligation strands (written security program, provider safeguarding conditions, disclosure and consent limits on return information, state duties, incident path) and fixes the standing decisions on systems, individual credentials, transmission channels and seasonal access removal

competency_questions.question: Which client segment should the practice commit to, what does a return in that segment actually cost in work, and what makes the commitment expensive to reverse?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SEGMENT_CANDIDATE_MAP describes candidates by document pattern, arrival timing and incumbent alternative; RETURN_COMPLEXITY_SIGNATURE gives each a work signature with a minutes distribution including its long tail; SEGMENT_COMMITMENT_DECISION records the choice, the compounding it buys, the concentration risk and the evidence that would reverse it

competency_questions.question: Office, virtual or hybrid - how does the delivery model change what the practice can hold and what it can finish in the peak weeks?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SERVICE_MODEL_CHOICE states what each model buys and costs in visibility, interruption load, geography and throughput ceiling, and ties the choice to the committed segment's observed behaviour rather than the owner's preference

competency_questions.question: How do I choose preparation software and the systems around it, and when in the year must that decision be finished?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SOFTWARE_STACK_SELECTION orders the evaluation as form coverage for the committed segment first, then the licensing mechanism with a break-even the practice computes from its own expected mix, then the supporting layer, and requires installation, prior-year conversion and rehearsal before intake opens

competency_questions.question: What is this practice's seasonal demand curve, what moves its shape, and how do I observe my own instead of assuming the industry's?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEMAND_CURVE_MECHANISM names the phases of the season, the forces that move each phase, and the per-return arrival and completion logging that lets the practice rebuild its own curve each season

competency_questions.question: How many returns can this practice actually finish in its peak weeks, what constraint binds first, and what happens to work that arrives after that?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PEAK_CAPACITY_MODEL produces a peak-week ceiling with a named binding constraint and an explicit rework reserve; PEAK_INTAKE_CUTOFF_RULE supplies the published cutoff dates, the document-completeness condition, the extension path offered instead and the named override authority

competency_questions.question: How does money move through a year in which revenue arrives in a few weeks and costs run all twelve months, and how is the fee actually collected?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SEASONAL_COST_AND_CASHFLOW_SHAPE separates year-round commitments from volume-scaling costs and derives a measured off-season reserve from a due-date-versus-collection schedule; FEE_COLLECTION_MECHANISM states the collection ladder and the plain-disclosure duty attached to refund-funded products

competency_questions.question: How is the fee for a given return constructed, how is it quoted before work starts, and what happens when the return turns out to be more complex than what was quoted?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PRICING_ARCHITECTURE chooses the fee-construction mechanism from the return's real work drivers and forbids refund amount as an input; COMPLEXITY_TIER_LADDER defines tiers by intake-recognisable triggers; QUOTE_AND_REPRICING_RULE requires a written pre-work quote, a stop-and-re-quote trigger with client approval, and a stated concession authority

competency_questions.question: What must be verified before the practice opens for a season, and what does the finished season's own record change for the next one?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SEASON_READINESS_GATE lists the dated, owned go/no-go items across authorizations, systems, pricing and capacity with open risks named rather than assumed away; SEASON_ECONOMICS_RECALIBRATION compares planned against realized mix, minutes, ceiling, fees, curve and costs and forces an explicit change-or-accept decision per divergence

glossary.definition: The compressed annual window in which the great majority of a preparation practice's returns arrive, are prepared and are transmitted; in this knowledge base it is the operating period against which capacity, cash flow and pricing are all measured, and its exact dates are read from the tax authority's current calendar rather than assumed.

The obligation class requiring any person compensated for preparing a federal return to obtain a preparer identifier, place it on returns they prepare, and renew it on the authority's cadence; treated here as a class whose current mechanics, eligibility and renewal window must be verified with the authority each season.

Firm-level authorization to transmit returns electronically, granted after an application including an identity and suitability review; it belongs to the firm and its principals, is not transferable, must be kept current as the firm changes, and its current application mechanics and timing must be confirmed with the authority.

The authority to act for a taxpayer before the tax authority in matters beyond preparing the return - examinations, appeals, collection contacts - which the fully credentialed classes hold broadly and other preparer classes hold in limited form or not at all; the boundary between preparing and representing is the practice's referral line.

The preparer-facing requirement attached to certain refundable credits and filing statuses to ask adequate questions, not ignore contradictory information, document what was asked and answered, and retain that record, with a per-return penalty class attached to failure; the credits in scope and the required record change and are verified against current rules.

This knowledge base's term for the concrete shape of one segment's typical return: the schedules and form classes it carries, the number of source documents and how many arrive late or wrong, the interview-versus-data-entry split, states, prior-year continuity, review depth, and the distribution of preparer minutes including the long tail.

A priced band of return defined by triggers recognisable at intake - an added state, a rental, a business, a due-diligence interview class - rather than by an outcome discovered at the end; the unit a quote is issued from before work begins.

The distribution across the season of when returns arrive rather than when they are finished: an early refund-motivated wave, a mid-season plateau, a deadline crush and a tail of extended and corrected work; the practice's central planning object and the thing it logs to rebuild each year.

A third-party arrangement in which a client's refund is routed through an intermediary that deducts the preparation fee and its own product fees before forwarding the balance; a real client-borne cost that must be disclosed plainly and in advance and never presented as the preparation fee being free or painless.

The published date and document-completeness condition after which new work is no longer promised for the original deadline and is scheduled onto a properly explained extension path instead; a policy set before the season rather than a refusal improvised during it.

nodes.definition: Fix what the practice actually sells before anything is registered, leased or advertised: the preparation and filing of a defined class of tax returns for a defined class of clients, priced per return, delivered inside a compressed season that repeats each year with largely the same people. The charter names the revenue unit as one completed, signed, accepted return - not a billable hour and not a subscription - so that pricing, capacity, staffing and cash planning are all denominated in the same thing. It names the season as the operating period the practice lives on, names the annually returning client base as the asset each season builds, and writes down the three things the practice will never sell: a promised refund outcome, a position the documentation cannot support, and advice on an individual taxpayer's situation that its authorization class does not permit it to give. The charter also carries the practice's honest epistemic limit: every requirement class it touches - preparer identification, e-file authorization, state registration, credit due-diligence duties, taxpayer-data protection - is named as a class to be verified in current form with the relevant authority in the practice's own jurisdiction, because these rules move between seasons and a charter built on remembered rules is a charter built on sand.

included: the revenue unit and what counts as one unit of work
the season as the operating period
the returning-client premise the practice is built on
the never-sell list
the standing instruction to verify every named requirement class currently and locally
excluded: the per-return production pipeline and its controls, owned by the return workflow knowledge base
retention mechanics and off-season revenue lines, owned by the returning-client knowledge base
any conclusion about a specific taxpayer's facts

pros.claim: Denominating everything in one accepted return makes capacity, price and cash planning speak the same language instead of arguing in different currencies
pros.example: a peak plan expressed as returns finishable per week, which is what makes an intake cutoff computable at all

cons.claim: A per-return charter makes income structurally lumpy and creates constant pressure to fill the calendar with work outside the practice's competence
cons.example: accepting a first multi-state partnership return in late March because the charter never said which returns are out of scope

failure_modes: leaving the revenue unit vague so pricing is argued in hours while capacity is argued in returns
writing a charter that quietly promises an outcome (a bigger refund, a faster refund) instead of a piece of work
treating the requirement classes named in the charter as settled facts rather than as things to re-verify before each season
acceptance_tests: the charter states the revenue unit, the client class, the season boundary and the never-sell list in writing and is dated
every regulatory class the charter names carries an explicit instruction to verify it with the authority in the practice's own jurisdiction before relying on it
revisit_triggers: the owner adds a return type or client class the charter never named
a rule change alters what the practice may sign, file or say about its own services

base.update_signal: the owner restates the client class, the return types the practice will sign, or what the practice claims in its marketing

nodes.definition: Map the classes of authorization a paid preparer can hold and record which class each person in the practice actually holds, because the class decides what may be signed, what may be represented, and what must be handed to somebody else. The classes to keep distinct are: the paid-preparer identification obligation that attaches to anyone compensated for preparing a federal return and that must be renewed on the authority's cadence; the unenrolled preparer class, which carries the narrowest practice rights; voluntary filing-season education programs that confer a limited standing short of full credentials; and the fully credentialed classes - enrolled agent, certified public accountant, attorney - which carry broad representation rights before the tax authority. For each person the map records how the class was obtained, its renewal date and continuing-education obligation class, the sanction exposure attached to it, and the exact line between preparing a return and representing a taxpayer in an examination, appeal or collection matter. Nothing here is taken from memory or from what another preparer says: eligibility rules, renewal windows, program names and fees change, so each item is confirmed against the authority's or the credentialing body's own current publication before the practice depends on it.

included: the authorization class each preparer holds and its current status
renewal and continuing-education obligation classes
the prepare-versus-represent boundary
a written referral rule for work above the class
excluded: state-level preparer registration and multi-state authority, which has its own unit
the in-return decision to research or escalate a specific technical question, owned by the return workflow knowledge base
any assertion of current fees, exam content or renewal dates as fact

pros.claim: A recorded class boundary converts a dangerous improvised favour into a documented referral that protects both the client and the preparer
pros.example: an examination notice routed to a credentialed colleague under a standing arrangement instead of being answered by an unenrolled preparer

cons.claim: The credential ladder takes months or years to climb, so a practice that discovers mid-season that it needs representation standing cannot acquire it in time
cons.example: a client who receives a notice in March whose preparer has neither the standing to act nor a referral relationship in place

failure_modes: operating on last season's understanding of a renewal or education requirement
blurring preparation and representation in marketing language so clients expect help the class cannot provide
letting an identification credential lapse between seasons and preparing returns anyway
acceptance_tests: every person who will be compensated for preparing a return has their authorization class, current status and renewal date recorded before intake opens
the practice can name one concrete example of work its class must refer out and the destination it refers it to
revisit_triggers: a renewal window or continuing-education deadline approaches
the authority changes preparer identification or education program mechanics
a preparer begins or completes a credentialing path

base.update_signal: the authority publishes a change to preparer identification, education programs or practice rights, or a preparer's class or status changes

nodes.definition: Work out separately from federal standing what each state and locality the practice touches demands of it, because several states impose their own preparer registration, education, examination, bonding or client-disclosure obligation classes on top of the federal ones, and a preparer who obliges a neighbour with an out-of-state return can walk straight into a requirement nobody checked. This unit inventories the states in which the practice's clients actually file - residence, part-year moves, non-resident work states, entity registration states - and, for each, the preparer-facing obligation class, the state's own electronic filing enrollment or acceptance rules, and any disclosure or engagement-terms duty. It also covers the registrations the practice needs simply to be a business: entity or trade-name registration class, local business licence class, and the professional liability coverage decision that no rule may compel but that the exposure argues for. The output is a short, dated list of states the practice will prepare for, each with its requirement class satisfied and its verification date, plus a written refusal-and-referral path for states not on the list. Every item is read from that state's own tax agency or licensing board publications, never inferred from federal standing.

included: the dated served-states list and the requirement class satisfied per state
state electronic filing enrollment as distinct from federal acceptance
the practice's own business registration and coverage decisions
the refusal path for an unserved state
excluded: federal credential classes, which have their own unit
how a multi-state return is actually allocated and prepared, owned by the return workflow knowledge base
any claim that a named state does or does not require registration today

pros.claim: A dated served-states list turns an unbounded compliance surface into a small checkable one that a front desk can apply without judgement
pros.example: a walk-in whose return needs a state the practice has not enrolled in being referred out at the counter rather than discovered mid-preparation

cons.claim: Restricting served states costs real revenue in a mobile client base and can cost a whole household over one member's work location
cons.example: a couple where one spouse commutes across a state line the practice does not serve, so both returns go elsewhere

failure_modes: assuming federal standing covers state preparer obligations
adding a state mid-season because one client asked and never registering for it
letting a state registration, bond or enrollment lapse quietly between seasons
acceptance_tests: the served-states list exists with a verification date and the satisfied requirement class named for each state
at least one written refusal-and-referral path exists for a state not on the list
revisit_triggers: a client moves, takes work in a new state, or the practice considers a new market
a state announces a preparer registration, bonding or electronic filing enrollment change

base.update_signal: a state publishes a change to preparer registration or filing enrollment, or the client base's filing footprint moves

nodes.definition: Treat authorization to transmit returns electronically as the long-lead prerequisite it is rather than a setting inside the software. A practice filing returns for compensation generally has to be accepted as an authorized electronic filing provider through an application that includes identity and suitability review of the firm and its principals, and that review consumes calendar time measured in weeks to months - which places the application squarely in the off-season, several months before the first document arrives. This unit tracks the whole path: the application and its identity steps; the fact that the authorization belongs to the firm and its principals, is not transferable and must be updated when principals, name, structure or address change; the electronic filing mandate class that applies to preparers above a volume threshold and therefore removes paper as a fallback for a growing practice; the state-level filing enrollment that may sit on top of federal acceptance; and the standing habit of watching the transmission account for volume anomalies that would signal misuse of the practice's credentials. Because acceptance criteria, thresholds, monitoring tools and timing all change, each item is confirmed against the authority's current published process before a season is planned around it.

included: the authorization application and its lead time
firm-level ownership and the duty to keep it current
the volume-based filing mandate class
state filing enrollment layered on federal acceptance
transmission-account monitoring for credential misuse
excluded: how an individual return is assembled and transmitted, owned by the return workflow knowledge base
software selection, which is a separate decision
any statement of current thresholds, processing times or application fees as fact

pros.claim: Starting the application in the off-season removes the single most common reason a new practice cannot open on time
pros.example: a practice that applies in summer and has a live test transmission completed before any client documents arrive

cons.claim: The authorization ties the practice's ability to operate at all to an external review it cannot accelerate or appeal quickly
cons.example: a suitability question that pauses an application while the calendar runs toward the season

failure_modes: planning a first season around an authorization that has not yet been granted
failing to update the authorization when principals, firm name or address change
never checking transmission volumes, so credential misuse is discovered by the authority rather than by the practice
acceptance_tests: the authorization is granted and a live test transmission has completed before intake opens
a named person checks the transmission account on a stated cadence through the season and records that they did
revisit_triggers: a principal, address, firm name or ownership structure changes
the authority changes application, mandate-threshold or monitoring mechanics

base.update_signal: the authority changes provider application, mandate or monitoring mechanics, or the firm's principals or details change

nodes.definition: Draw the line, in the off-season and in writing, between the return situations this practice is competent to sign and those it will decline or refer - at the level of return classes, never at the level of an individual client's facts. The perimeter is three lists. Accepted: the return shapes the practice can prepare and review well, such as wage-earner returns with standard credits, a stated depth of self-employment or rental activity, and the states on its served list. Conditional: shapes accepted only with a named extra control - a second reviewer, a longer appointment, a research step booked before the work - which typically covers multi-state allocations, first-year entity returns, equity compensation, digital-asset dispositions and foreign account or foreign income reporting classes. Referred out: representation matters above the practice's credential class, deep prior-year non-filer reconstruction, and anything that needs a legal opinion. The perimeter exists because signing a return is a personal assertion by a named preparer, and the honest limit of that person's competence is a decision best made calmly in July rather than at eleven o'clock on an April night with a client waiting.

included: the accepted, conditional and referred-out class lists
the named extra control that makes a conditional class acceptable
named referral destinations
the rule for expanding the perimeter and who may do it
excluded: the in-return decision to research, escalate or decline a specific ambiguous item mid-engagement, owned by the return workflow knowledge base
tax conclusions on any specific taxpayer's facts
the client-retention consequences of a decline, owned by the returning-client knowledge base

pros.claim: A written perimeter makes declining fast, calm and impersonal at exactly the moment it is hardest to say no
pros.example: a walk-in with a foreign rental property met with a prepared referral instead of an improvised yes in the second week of April

cons.claim: A perimeter drawn tightly in year one leaves capable higher-fee revenue on the table and can stall the practice's growth into better work
cons.example: turning away a straightforward first small-entity return the preparer could have handled with one scheduled review

failure_modes: expanding the perimeter silently under peak-season revenue pressure
writing a perimeter so vague that every unusual return lands in the conditional list
keeping a conditional list without naming who performs the extra control that makes it conditional
acceptance_tests: the three lists exist and each conditional class names the specific control that makes it acceptable
every referred-out class names at least one destination the practice has actually spoken to
revisit_triggers: the practice hires or loses the person whose skill defined a perimeter line
a repeated decline pattern shows a class worth learning before the next season

base.update_signal: the practice gains or loses a competence, or a season's decline log shows a class it repeatedly turns away

nodes.definition: Constrain how this practice is permitted to sell before a single word of marketing is written, because preparation is bought under deadline pressure by people who mostly cannot evaluate the work and who are, in a meaningful share of cases, financially stressed. Four standing rules carry refusal consequences. First, refund-neutral selling: the practice advertises the work - accurate preparation, a real review, filing, a named person who is still there next year - and never a refund size, a comparison with what another preparer got someone, or a fee that moves with the refund. Second, no fear-selling: penalty, notice and examination exposure may be explained factually when it is relevant to a decision the client is actually making, but never used as an urgency lever to close a sale or add a tier. Third, vulnerable-filer care: elderly clients, clients with limited English, first-time filers and clients in acute financial distress get slower explanation, a plain statement of the fee and what it buys, a comprehension check, and no product they did not ask for. Fourth, position neutrality: the practice never competes by implying a more aggressive treatment of a deduction or credit than the documentation will support. These are the offer's boundary conditions, not its tone.

included: refund-neutral claims in every channel
the ban on fear-driven urgency
the vulnerable-filer slow lane and comprehension check
position neutrality in competitive selling
what the practice refuses to say even when a competitor says it
excluded: the accuracy controls and documentation that make a position defensible in the first place, owned by the return workflow knowledge base
retention and referral programs aimed at the existing base, owned by the returning-client knowledge base
advice about any specific taxpayer's position

pros.claim: A promise about work rather than outcome is one the practice can keep every year, which is precisely the mechanism that produces a returning base
pros.example: advertising a named preparer and a written quote before work starts rather than a refund figure nobody can guarantee

cons.claim: It concedes the loudest part of the market to competitors advertising refund outcomes and instant money, and costs visible walk-in volume in the early weeks
cons.example: a storefront across the street promising the biggest refund in town while this practice advertises a quote-first process

failure_modes: letting the fee move with refund size in any disguised form
using audit or penalty fear as the lever that closes an add-on sale
processing a distressed or confused client at peak-season speed with no comprehension check
acceptance_tests: no published or spoken offer references refund size, and no fee formula anywhere in the practice takes refund amount as an input
a named slow-lane rule exists for clients who need more explanation time, and staff can state it
revisit_triggers: a competitor's refund-based claim creates internal pressure to match it
a complaint, confusion or cancellation pattern appears in a vulnerable client group

base.update_signal: a complaint pattern, a regulator advisory on preparer advertising, or internal pressure to match a competitor's outcome claim

nodes.definition: Treat the preparer due-diligence duties that attach to certain refundable credits and filing statuses as an input to practice design rather than as paperwork discovered at the desk in February. Certain claims - the earned-income class of refundable credits, child and dependent related credits, education credits and head-of-household status among them - carry an explicit obligation class on the preparer: ask adequate questions, do not ignore information that contradicts what you are told, document what was asked and answered, and retain that record for a stated period, with a per-return penalty class attached to failure. The design consequences are concrete and measurable: a segment heavy in these claims costs more preparer minutes than its form count suggests, needs people trained to conduct an interview rather than to type numbers, justifies its own price rung, lengthens the appointment, and raises the practice's exposure on every one of those returns. This unit decides how much of that exposure the practice will carry, at what price, with what training, and where the limit is - including the honest option of not building a base concentrated in the highest-exposure claim class. The credits in scope, the required record and the penalty class all change and are verified against current rules every season.

included: the obligation class as a cost, price, training and exposure input
the practice's stated appetite and limit for credit-heavy work
the interview-capable staffing requirement it implies
the standing duty to re-verify the class each season
excluded: the per-return due-diligence checklist, its documentation habit and its retention workflow, owned by the return workflow and documentation knowledge base
judging whether any particular taxpayer qualifies for any particular credit
penalty amounts or credit parameters stated as current fact

pros.claim: Pricing and staffing the due-diligence load up front stops the practice from selling interview-heavy returns at data-entry prices
pros.example: a segment where most returns carry a refundable-credit interview being booked into longer appointment slots and priced on its own rung

cons.claim: Carrying the exposure concentrates penalty and reputational risk in the client group least able to absorb a rejected claim, and the required questioning can feel intrusive to honest long-standing clients
cons.example: a client of many years asked again for evidence about a child they have always claimed, and hearing it as suspicion

failure_modes: treating due-diligence questions as a form to be signed rather than an interview to be conducted
quoting credit-heavy returns on form count alone and losing the interview minutes
building a client base concentrated in the highest-exposure claim class without the training or price to support it
acceptance_tests: the practice can state which claim classes trigger the obligation and what its own per-return time and price allowance for them is
a training step exists and is dated for everyone who will conduct those interviews
revisit_triggers: the authority updates the credits in scope, the required documentation or the penalty class
the season's realized mix shifts materially toward credit-heavy returns

base.update_signal: the authority revises the credits in scope, the required questions or the penalty class, or the practice's realized claim mix shifts

nodes.definition: Stand up the data-protection infrastructure the practice is obliged to have before a single client document arrives, because a preparation practice holds the densest identity package a household possesses: names, taxpayer identification numbers, dates of birth, bank routing details, employer records and the income history of every member of the family. The obligation class has several strands, each to be verified in current form: a written information security program duty that attaches to preparers, the safeguarding conditions attached to being an authorized electronic filing provider, the rules governing use or disclosure of taxpayer return information for anything other than preparing the return - which is what makes cross-selling and list-sharing a compliance question rather than a marketing one - state data-protection and breach-notification duties, and the practice's own incident path if credentials or data are compromised. What belongs to this unit is the standing procurement and configuration decision: which systems hold client data, how access is granted and removed including for seasonal staff, how documents are transmitted and why never through unsecured personal email or messaging, how devices are managed, and what is written down and dated. What does not belong here is how any individual return's documents are handled once the season is running.

included: the written program and who owns it
which systems hold client data and how they are chosen
individual credentials, access grant and removal for seasonal staff
permitted transmission channels and the refusal of unsecured ones
the incident path and who executes it
excluded: per-return document handling and workflow security practice during the season, owned by the return workflow knowledge base
legal interpretation of any specific breach obligation, which needs qualified counsel
any claim about what a named jurisdiction currently requires

pros.claim: Deciding systems and access rules before the season means seasonal help can be onboarded and offboarded cleanly instead of through improvised credential sharing
pros.example: a temporary preparer given a named account with preparation-only access and a removal date set the week they start

cons.claim: Real security infrastructure carries year-round cost and daily friction in a business whose revenue arrives in a few weeks
cons.example: paying for a managed portal, storage and device management through a summer in which almost no returns are prepared

failure_modes: accepting client documents through unsecured personal email or messaging because a client found it easier
sharing one software login across seasonal staff so no action can be attributed or revoked
having no written program and no incident path until the day something goes wrong
acceptance_tests: the written program exists, is dated, names every system holding client data and names the person accountable for it
every person with access holds an individual credential with a recorded grant date and a removal date
revisit_triggers: seasonal staff are hired or leave
a system is added or replaced, or a vendor discloses an incident
the obligation class is updated by the authority or by a state the practice serves

base.update_signal: a change in the security program or safeguarding obligation class, a staffing change, a system replacement, or any incident anywhere in the practice's supply chain

nodes.definition: Inventory the client segments this practice could serve and describe each one as a piece of business rather than as a demographic. The candidates worth keeping separate include: wage-earner households with standard credits, which arrive in volume, file early and shop on price; itemizing and investment households, whose statements arrive later, whose documents are more numerous and whose tolerance for a considered fee is higher; self-employed and gig filers, who bring bookkeeping-shaped disorder and quarterly obligations that create contact outside the season; rental and small real-estate owners, whose depreciation and basis continuity makes the prior-year file itself valuable; small-business entity clients, whose returns carry earlier deadlines and pull owner returns along behind them; and occupational, employer or language communities that cut across all of the above and behave like referral networks. For each candidate the map records where those clients already are, who currently prepares for them and why, the document pattern they arrive with, when in the season they arrive, and what makes them leave a preparer. The map is deliberately wider than the practice will serve: its job is to turn the later commitment into a choice between described options instead of a drift toward whoever happens to walk through the door.

included: candidate segments described by document pattern, arrival timing and switching behaviour
the incumbent alternative each segment currently uses
referral density and community structure where it exists
excluded: the commitment decision itself, which is a separate unit
referral programs and retention campaigns aimed at clients already served, owned by the returning-client knowledge base
market-size or share figures, which this knowledge base does not invent

pros.claim: Describing segments by document pattern and arrival timing rather than by income or age makes them comparable on the only axes that change the practice's work
pros.example: comparing a gig-worker segment with an entity segment by when their documents are actually complete rather than by what they earn

cons.claim: Mapping segments the practice cannot serve consumes scarce off-season time and seeds ambition beyond the competence perimeter
cons.example: a detailed map of an expatriate filer segment built by a preparer with no foreign-reporting competence and no path to it

failure_modes: describing segments as demographics with no implication for the work
mapping only the segment the owner personally resembles
confusing a marketing channel with a segment
acceptance_tests: each candidate carries an arrival-timing note, a document pattern and a named incumbent alternative
at least one candidate outside the owner's own demographic is described
revisit_triggers: a large local employer, community or competitor changes materially
a season's walk-in and enquiry log shows a segment the map never described

base.update_signal: the enquiry log, a local employer change, or a competitor's move reveals a segment the map does not describe

nodes.definition: Convert each candidate segment into the concrete shape of the work one of its returns demands, because that shape - not the client's income and not the number of pages - is what the practice staffs and sells. A signature records, for a typical return in the segment: which schedules and form classes appear; how many source documents must be collected and what share of them typically arrive late, duplicated or corrected; how much of the work is interview and chase versus data entry; whether a due-diligence interview class attaches; how many states are involved; whether prior-year continuity such as depreciation, carryforwards or basis must be carried forward or reconstructed; the depth of review a second pair of eyes needs; and the realistic distribution of preparer minutes, explicitly including the long tail in which a minority of returns absorb several times the median. Signatures are built from the practice's own job records wherever those exist and are marked as estimates where they do not, because a signature borrowed from somebody else's practice is the fastest route to a mispriced tier and an unachievable capacity plan.

included: form and schedule shape per segment
document count and the late or corrected share
interview and chase minutes as distinct from preparation minutes
review depth
the minutes distribution and its long tail, labelled estimated or observed
excluded: how the work is actually executed and controlled inside a return, owned by the return workflow knowledge base
the price attached to the signature, which is a downstream decision
any minutes figure presented as an industry norm

pros.claim: A minutes distribution with its long tail, rather than a comfortable average, is what lets a price tier and a capacity ceiling survive contact with real returns
pros.example: a self-employment segment whose median return is quick but whose worst quartile reliably absorbs a whole evening

cons.claim: Before a season exists the signature must be estimated from thin evidence, and an over-confident estimate hardens into a mispriced tier that is awkward to correct with existing clients
cons.example: a first-year guess at review time for entity returns that proves badly low once the first ones are actually reviewed

failure_modes: averaging the long tail away and planning as if every return is the median
measuring preparation time while ignoring document-chasing and client-response time
reusing another practice's numbers as if they were observations of this one
acceptance_tests: each served segment has a signature with a document count, an interview-versus-entry split and a minutes range explicitly labelled estimated or observed
the long tail is described rather than only the median
revisit_triggers: a season's job records contradict the signature
a form, credit or reporting change alters the work a segment's return requires

base.update_signal: logged minutes and document counts from a completed season, or a form or credit change that reshapes a segment's return

nodes.definition: Choose the practice's primary segment and at most one adjacent segment, and write down what the choice costs to reverse. The decision weighs each candidate's work signature against the competence perimeter, the due-diligence exposure the practice is willing to carry, where the segment's returns sit on the calendar, and the compounding that depth in one segment produces: the same document set arriving every year, interview checklists that stop changing, a preparer who recognises the segment's recurring issues on sight, review that accelerates because the errors repeat, and referral density inside a community whose members talk to each other. Against that stands concentration risk - one employer restructuring, one industry contracting, one rule change reshaping the niche's returns - and the plain fact that commitment is expensive to unwind, because software modules, marketing, learning and local reputation are all bought against it. The decision is recorded with the evidence that would reverse it and the season in which it may legitimately be reopened, so that it is not re-litigated at the worst possible moment by a single persuasive client in March.

included: the primary and adjacent segment choice
the compounding mechanism depth buys
concentration risk and its watch signals
reversal cost and the evidence that would justify reversing
the season in which the decision may be reopened
excluded: retention programs and referral engines run against the existing base, owned by the returning-client knowledge base
off-season service lines built for a segment, owned by the same knowledge base
any claim about a segment's size or profitability drawn from outside the practice

pros.claim: Depth in one segment compounds every season because the same document set trains the checklist, the preparer and the reviewer simultaneously
pros.example: a trade-specific practice whose third-season returns are recognised and reviewed markedly faster than its first-season ones

cons.claim: Commitment concentrates the practice's risk in one community and one rule set, and both can move without warning
cons.example: a niche built around a single large local employer that restructures between two seasons

failure_modes: committing to a segment whose work signature was never measured or even estimated
serving every segment poorly instead of one segment well
reopening the commitment mid-season under pressure from one attractive client
acceptance_tests: the commitment names the primary segment, the adjacent one, the reversal cost and the evidence that would change it
the decision is dated and assigned the season in which it will be reviewed
revisit_triggers: a season's realized mix diverges materially from the committed segment
a rule change or an employer change reshapes the niche's returns or its population

base.update_signal: realized segment mix at season end, or a structural change in the committed community or its rule set

nodes.definition: Decide how clients and their documents physically reach the practice, because that single choice sets the cost base, the peak throughput ceiling and the client group the practice is able to hold. An office model buys walk-in visibility, drop-off convenience and the reassurance of a street address, and pays for it with a year-round lease, front-desk labour precisely during the weeks when the telephone never stops, and a ceiling set by chairs and appointment slots. A virtual model runs on a secure portal, electronic signature and remote identity verification, erases geography from the addressable base, and trades that for a colder acquisition path, a client group that must be willing and able to upload documents, and a much higher burden of proof on security and responsiveness. A hybrid keeps a small appointment space or a scheduled drop-off window in front of a portal-first process, which is often the honest answer for a mixed base but doubles the number of paths that must be designed and staffed. The choice is made against the committed segment's observed behaviour and against the peak week specifically, because the delivery model is the component that fails first when volume arrives.

included: what each model buys and costs in visibility, interruption load, geography and ceiling
the peak-week interruption rule that protects preparation blocks
the client-facing steps each model obliges and who walks them before the season
excluded: the security program the chosen model obliges, which has its own unit
the intake and document-collection procedure inside a return, owned by the return workflow knowledge base
lease terms, rents or fit-out costs stated as market figures

pros.claim: A portal-first model converts the peak's worst constraint - unscheduled interruption - into asynchronous work that can be batched into blocks
pros.example: documents arriving overnight into a queue instead of clients arriving at the desk in the middle of a review

cons.claim: Removing the physical touchpoint removes the trust signal some segments buy on and shifts acquisition onto channels the practice must build from nothing
cons.example: an older client base that never completes a portal upload and quietly drifts back to a storefront preparer

failure_modes: choosing the model from the owner's preference rather than the committed segment's behaviour
running an office model with no appointment discipline so walk-ins destroy every preparation block
promising virtual convenience without the identity-verification, signature and support infrastructure to deliver it
acceptance_tests: the model is stated together with the peak-week interruption rule that protects preparation time
every client-facing step of the chosen model has been walked end to end by someone in the practice before intake opens
revisit_triggers: the committed segment shifts or a new adjacent segment is added
a season shows a document-return path a meaningful share of clients will not use

base.update_signal: observed portal adoption, walk-in volume and interruption counts from a completed season

nodes.definition: Select the professional preparation software and the systems around it during the off-season, treating the choice as a commitment for at least a full season that cannot be unwound once live returns exist inside it. The evaluation has a fixed order. Form and schedule coverage for the committed segment comes first: a package that does not handle the entity, state or specialty forms the segment needs is disqualified whatever it costs. Then the licensing mechanism: pay-per-return pricing that scales with volume against an unlimited licence with a fixed seasonal cost, where the break-even is not a number anybody else can supply - the practice computes it from its own expected mix and volume and re-computes it after the season. Then the supporting layer: electronic signature, client portal, document storage and retention, conversion of prior-year client files, multi-user access control that matches the security program, and the vendor's support responsiveness during exactly the weeks when every one of its customers needs support at once. The stack must be installed, updated, conversion-tested against real prior-year data and rehearsed on practice returns before intake opens, because a package learned during a peak costs more in errors and lost minutes than any licence saves.

included: form coverage screening against the committed segment
the licensing mechanism and the practice's own break-even computation
the supporting layer of signature, portal, storage and access control
prior-year conversion and pre-season rehearsal
excluded: how the software is used to prepare and review an individual return, owned by the return workflow knowledge base
vendor prices, discounts or feature comparisons stated as fact
the security program itself, which sets the requirements this selection must satisfy

pros.claim: Computing the per-return against flat-licence break-even from the practice's own expected mix turns a sales pitch into arithmetic the owner controls
pros.example: a first season at low volume where per-return pricing is cheaper, with the break-even re-checked the moment volume grows

cons.claim: Switching packages later forces conversion of client history and retraining into the same short off-season, and conversions lose detail that has to be re-entered by hand
cons.example: depreciation and carryforward continuity that must be checked line by line after a mid-life conversion

failure_modes: choosing on price before confirming form coverage for the committed segment
installing and learning the package after intake has already opened
leaving prior-year conversion untested until the first returning client arrives
acceptance_tests: form and schedule coverage for the committed segment is verified against the package before purchase, in writing
a prior-year conversion and a live test filing are both completed before intake opens
revisit_triggers: volume crosses the licence break-even the practice computed
the committed segment gains a form class the package handles poorly
the vendor changes pricing, support terms or ownership

base.update_signal: realized return volume against the computed break-even, a vendor terms change, or a coverage gap found during the season

nodes.definition: Decide how money actually moves from client to practice, because the collection mechanism changes both the cash curve and the ethics of the sale. The options form a ladder. Payment at delivery before the return is transmitted is the simplest and protects the practice, but requires the client to have money before their refund exists. Card or electronic payment at signature adds convenience at a processing cost. A deposit at intake with the balance at delivery filters non-serious work and funds the season's early weeks, at the cost of a harder first conversation. Refund-funded products - the bank-product class in which a third party receives the refund, deducts the preparation fee plus its own product fees and forwards the balance - make preparation reachable for clients who genuinely have no cash in February, and carry a specific and non-negotiable obligation with them: the client pays real money for that convenience, the cost is stated plainly and in advance, the arrangement is never described as the fee being free or simply taken out of the refund, and it is never the default offered to a client who could just pay. The practice writes down which mechanisms it offers, in what order it presents them, and the one thing it will never do - let its own fee vary with the size of the refund.

included: the collection ladder and the order options are presented in
the plain-disclosure duty attached to refund-funded products
deposit policy and its effect on early-season cash
the standing prohibition on refund-linked fees
excluded: debt collection from clients who never pay, and any legal process attached to it
the accounting treatment of collected fees against work in progress
any statement of what a named product currently charges

pros.claim: Collecting at or before delivery removes the practice's largest invisible cost, which is chasing fees from clients whose refund has already been spent
pros.example: a return held for transmission until the agreed fee is settled, with that condition stated plainly at quoting time rather than discovered at pickup

cons.claim: Requiring payment up front excludes exactly the clients for whom the refund is the only available money, and pushes them toward whoever sells a refund-funded product hardest
cons.example: a household that cannot pay in February and books with a competitor advertising no money up front

failure_modes: defaulting every client into a refund-funded product because it is the easiest sale to make
quoting a preparation fee without naming the additional product cost the client will bear
allowing any collection arrangement in which the practice's own fee moves with the refund amount
acceptance_tests: every offered mechanism is written down with its client-borne cost disclosed before the client chooses between them
no mechanism in use makes the practice's fee a function of the refund amount, and staff can state why
revisit_triggers: a product provider changes its fee structure or terms
collection failures or complaints cluster in one client group

base.update_signal: a change in product terms, a complaint pattern about disclosure, or realized collection timing from a completed season

nodes.definition: Model the season's arrival curve as the practice's central economic mechanism: nearly all revenue arrives inside a few weeks, the shape of those weeks is driven by forces the practice does not control, and every setup decision is a response to that shape. The curve has recognisable phases - an early wave of refund-motivated filers who arrive the moment employer and payer documents are issued; a mid-season plateau in which documents are complete and the work is most controllable and most profitable per hour; a deadline crush in which arrivals exceed any plausible capacity; and a tail of extended, corrected and late work that reaches into the following months. Its shape is moved by when payers issue documents, by statutory refund-release timing attached to certain credit classes, by entity deadlines that fall earlier than individual ones and pull owner returns with them, by corrected statements that arrive after the originals and reopen finished work, and by ordinary human procrastination. Because the curve is a mechanism and not a number, the practice must observe its own rather than assume the published pattern: log the arrival date, the segment and the completion date of every return and rebuild the curve each season. Capacity, staffing, cutoff, pricing and cash decisions are all downstream of that observed curve.

included: the phases of the season and what moves each one
how the committed segment's deadline positions shape the practice's own curve
the per-return arrival and completion log that makes the curve observable
the corrected-document tail that reopens completed work
excluded: deliberately smoothing demand into the off-season through extension, planning or bookkeeping lines, owned by the returning-client and off-season revenue knowledge base
any assertion of what a filing deadline or refund-release date currently is
the per-return handling of a corrected document, owned by the return workflow knowledge base

pros.claim: An arrival log turns the phrase everyone uses about being slammed in April into a distribution the next season can actually be planned against
pros.example: a practice that discovers its entity clients arrive weeks ahead of its individual ones and moves reviewer hours forward accordingly

cons.claim: The curve only becomes observable after a season has happened, so a first year must be planned on an assumed shape that will be wrong in its details
cons.example: a first-year plan built for a late crush that in fact arrives a fortnight earlier and finds the practice still hiring

failure_modes: planning capacity against the season's total volume instead of its heaviest week
assuming the published industry pattern is this practice's own pattern
ignoring the tail of corrected documents that reopens work already delivered and billed
acceptance_tests: arrival date, segment and completion date are captured for every return, not just the difficult ones
the season plan names the peak week explicitly rather than the season total
revisit_triggers: a deadline, refund-release rule or document-issuance practice changes
the realized curve differs materially from the one the season was planned against

base.update_signal: the arrival and completion log from a finished season, or a change in deadlines, refund timing or document issuance

nodes.definition: Compute what the practice can genuinely finish in its heaviest weeks and name the one constraint that binds first. Capacity is not the season's total hours divided by an average return: it is the number of returns that can pass every stage - intake, preparation, review, client signature, transmission - during the weeks when arrivals are heaviest, given that the same few people perform several of those stages and that client response time sits in the middle of the pipeline entirely outside the practice's control. The model is assembled from the committed segment's work signature including its long tail, the preparer and reviewer hours honestly available in those specific weeks after the owner's own selling, signing and client contact is subtracted, the interruption load the chosen delivery model permits, and a deliberate reserve for rework, corrected documents and the returns that simply go wrong. Its output is a peak-week return ceiling together with the named binding constraint - reviewer hours, appointment slots, client responsiveness or software seats - because knowing which one binds is what makes the next move obvious: hire, cut off intake, change the model, or reprice.

included: the peak-week return ceiling and how it is computed
the named binding constraint
the honest availability of owner and reviewer hours
an explicit reserve for rework and corrections
excluded: smoothing capacity across the year with off-season work, owned by the returning-client and off-season revenue knowledge base
the internal production controls that make throughput accurate, owned by the return workflow knowledge base
staffing rates or productivity benchmarks quoted from outside the practice

pros.claim: Naming the binding constraint converts a seasonal panic into a single decision with a known lever
pros.example: a practice that identifies review rather than preparation as its ceiling and buys reviewer hours instead of more intake

cons.claim: A ceiling computed from estimated minutes is fragile in a first season and will be either optimistic enough to hurt or conservative enough to waste capacity
cons.example: a ceiling built on median preparation time that collapses when a fifth of returns need a second round of client contact

failure_modes: planning to the season average and drowning in the peak week
counting owner hours as if the owner prepares full time and never sells, signs, answers or supervises
leaving no reserve, so the first wave of corrections consumes capacity that was already promised
acceptance_tests: the model states a peak-week return ceiling and names the constraint that binds first
a reserve for rework and late corrections is explicit rather than assumed
revisit_triggers: realized peak-week throughput differs materially from the modelled ceiling
the binding constraint changes after a hire, a model change or a segment shift

base.update_signal: realized peak-week completions, logged minutes per stage, and which constraint actually bound during the season

nodes.definition: Describe the practice's money as two curves that refuse to line up: revenue compressed into a short filing window and costs that run for twelve months. The cost side separates commitments that exist whether or not a single return is prepared - software licensing, portal and storage subscriptions, professional liability coverage, credential renewal and continuing education, any lease and its utilities, and the owner's own living costs - from the costs that scale with volume, such as seasonal preparer and front-desk labour, per-return software charges under a pay-per-return licence, printing, postage and card processing. The mechanism to internalise is the trough: the practice spends through the off-season on commitments made before the season, collects nearly everything within a few weeks, and must carry that surplus far enough forward to reach the next peak while also funding the next licence and any expansion. This unit builds the practice's own schedule of when each cost falls due against when fees are actually collected rather than earned, and treats the resulting minimum off-season reserve as a quantity to be measured from its own records - never a figure copied from another practice or an industry article.

included: the split between year-round commitments and volume-scaling costs
the due-date against collection-date schedule
the derived minimum off-season reserve
the distinction between fees collected and work actually finished
excluded: off-season revenue lines that would fill the trough with work, owned by the returning-client and off-season revenue knowledge base
tax and entity structuring for the practice itself, which needs its own qualified adviser
any cost, margin or reserve figure presented as an industry norm

pros.claim: Laying due dates against collection dates turns the off-season reserve from a hope into a computed requirement the owner can defend
pros.example: a licence renewal falling due months before the first fee of the next season is collected, visible on the schedule in advance

cons.claim: A reserve large enough to cover the trough is capital sitting idle through the months when it could have bought earlier marketing or a second seat
cons.example: holding funds through a summer in which an earlier hire would have raised the next peak's ceiling

failure_modes: treating peak-week cash as profit and spending it before the trough arrives
signing a year-round commitment on the strength of one unusually good season
forgetting that fees collected are not fees earned while returns are still open and reworkable
acceptance_tests: a twelve-month schedule of fixed commitments against expected collection timing exists and is dated
a stated minimum off-season reserve is derived from that schedule rather than asserted
revisit_triggers: a fixed commitment is added, repriced or renewed
a season's collections land materially outside the modelled timing

base.update_signal: actual collection dates and amounts against the schedule, or a change in any year-round commitment

nodes.definition: Decide in advance the date and the condition after which new work is no longer promised for the original deadline, and what is offered instead. Without a cutoff the deadline crush silently converts into accepted work the practice cannot finish accurately, and that is the precise point at which rushed signatures, quality failures and unpaid midnight hours happen. The rule has four parts. A stated cutoff date for new clients, and a separate later one for returning clients whose files, prior-year data and history the practice already holds. A completeness condition, so that a return whose documents are still incomplete by a stated date is treated as arriving after the cutoff however early its owner booked - because a booking is not a return. The alternative offered to everyone past the line, which is a properly explained filing-extension path including the plainly stated point that an extension of time to file is not an extension of any obligation to pay. And an exception rule naming who may override the cutoff, on what evidence, and where the override is logged. Publishing the cutoff before the season begins is what makes it a policy rather than a personal rejection.

included: separate cutoff dates for new and returning clients
the document-completeness condition
the extension path offered past the line and the payment point that must be explained with it
the named override authority and its log
excluded: the off-season economics of the extension book, its follow-through and the revenue it generates, owned by the returning-client and off-season revenue knowledge base
advising any specific taxpayer on their own payment position
the mechanics of preparing an extension, owned by the return workflow knowledge base

pros.claim: A published cutoff moves the hardest conversation of the season from April, when it is emotional, to January, when it can be written and rehearsed
pros.example: an intake page stating the date after which new work is scheduled onto an extension path, sent with every enquiry

cons.claim: A hard cutoff turns away late revenue a competitor will happily take, and late arrivals are disproportionately the complex, higher-fee returns
cons.example: a complex late arrival who becomes a competitor's best account for the next decade

failure_modes: setting a cutoff and then overriding it so often that it stops meaning anything
measuring the cutoff from the booking date rather than from document completeness
offering an extension without explaining that it does not extend an obligation to pay
acceptance_tests: the cutoff dates and the completeness condition are published before intake opens
the override authority is named and every override is logged with its reason
revisit_triggers: realized peak-week throughput shows the cutoff was set too early or far too late
the segment mix changes the arrival distribution enough to move the crush

base.update_signal: the count of overrides, the realized completion rate after the cutoff, and where the crush actually fell

nodes.definition: Choose the mechanism by which a fee comes to exist before choosing any amount at all. The candidate architectures behave differently under load. Per-form or per-schedule pricing assembles the fee from the return's components, scales automatically with complexity and is honest about the work, but stays opaque to the client until the work is finished. Flat pricing per return type is quotable in advance and easy to sell, but silently makes the tidy client subsidise the chaotic one. Complexity-tier pricing classifies returns into a small number of bands at intake and quotes from the band, which is the architecture that best satisfies the requirement to quote before working. Hourly pricing belongs only to cleanup and reconstruction work whose scope genuinely cannot be seen up front. A minimum fee protects the practice from returns too small to justify opening a file, and a returning-client structure decides in advance whether continuity is rewarded and how. The right architecture is the one whose inputs are the return's real work drivers - interview and chase time, review depth, states, prior-year continuity, due-diligence load - and whose inputs never include the refund. The amount itself is not something this knowledge base can supply: it is produced by the practice's own cost shape, the value of its scarce peak capacity and its local positioning, and it is tested every season against realized minutes per tier.

included: the candidate fee-construction mechanisms and their behaviour
the legitimate inputs to a fee and the forbidden one
the minimum-fee decision
how the architecture is tested against realized minutes
excluded: specific prices, price bands or competitor rates, which this knowledge base never invents
repricing an existing client base across seasons, owned by the returning-client knowledge base
discounting as a retention device, owned by the same knowledge base

pros.claim: An architecture whose inputs are the return's actual work drivers keeps price and effort correlated even as the client base drifts
pros.example: a fee that moves with an added state and an attached due-diligence interview rather than with what the client is getting back

cons.claim: Complexity-sensitive pricing is harder to advertise than a single headline number and invites comparison against simpler competitor offers that hide their extras
cons.example: a prospect weighing a banded quote against a storefront's advertised flat price that excludes the state return

failure_modes: setting price from a competitor's advertised figure without knowing what that figure includes
pricing on form count while interview, chase and review time drive the real cost
allowing any pricing input, discount or bonus that varies with refund size
acceptance_tests: the architecture can produce a quote before work begins for every accepted return class
no pricing input anywhere references refund amount
each tier's price is testable at season end against the minutes actually recorded against it
revisit_triggers: realized minutes per tier diverge from the assumption the price was built on
the cost base or the segment mix changes materially

base.update_signal: realized minutes and collected fee per tier from a completed season, or a material change in the cost base

nodes.definition: Build the small ladder of return tiers the practice quotes from, and define every rung by triggers that can be recognised at intake rather than discovered at delivery. A workable ladder has few enough rungs to explain in one sentence and triggers precise enough to classify a return from an intake questionnaire plus last year's file: a base rung for the simplest wage-earner return inside the perimeter; a rung for itemizing or investment activity; a rung for self-employment or rental activity, which usually carries the largest step because it drags bookkeeping-shaped work behind it; a rung or a named add-on for each additional state; a rung where a due-diligence interview class attaches and lengthens the appointment; and a top rung for entity returns and for reconstruction work priced on its own terms. Each rung states its trigger list, what is included, what is explicitly excluded, and which rung a return moves to when a trigger appears mid-work. The ladder's real test is not elegance but agreement: two different people in the practice, handed the same intake questionnaire, must classify it the same way.

included: the rungs and their intake-recognisable triggers
inclusions and exclusions per rung
the movement rule between rungs
the classification agreement test
excluded: the amounts attached to each rung, which come from the practice's own cost and capacity position
the in-return workflow that executes the tier's work, owned by the return workflow knowledge base
any published or benchmark tier structure quoted as standard practice

pros.claim: Triggers readable from an intake questionnaire let a quote be issued before a file is opened, which is what the honest-offer stance requires
pros.example: an intake question about rental property that moves a return one rung before any preparation time is spent

cons.claim: Every extra rung adds classification disputes and edge returns that sit defensibly in either of two tiers
cons.example: a single small brokerage statement that could reasonably be read into the base rung or the investment rung

failure_modes: defining tiers with vague adjectives such as simple or complex instead of triggers
building a ladder so granular that classifying a return takes longer than preparing it
having no stated rule for a return that straddles two rungs
acceptance_tests: two preparers independently classify the same set of sample intakes identically
every rung lists its triggers, its inclusions and its exclusions in writing
revisit_triggers: classification disagreements recur on the same kind of return
a new form class appears in the committed segment with no rung to hold it

base.update_signal: recurring classification disagreements, or a season's repricing events concentrated in one rung

nodes.definition: Fix how a price is communicated and what happens when the return turns out to be something other than what was quoted, which is the most common commercial failure in a preparation practice. The rule requires a written quote or a stated band before work begins, naming the tier, what it includes and the named extras that are not included - additional states, prior-year returns, amended filings, bookkeeping cleanup, expedited handling, and any product fee the client will bear. It then defines the repricing trigger: when preparation reveals a fact that moves the return up a rung - an undisclosed rental, a second state, a business the client described as a hobby, a carrier bag of unreconciled records - work stops, the client is told the new tier and price before that work is incurred, and explicit approval is recorded. The practice also decides its concession policy in advance: who may discount, within what limit and on what grounds, so that April exhaustion does not quietly become the pricing policy. None of this is a negotiation about the return's contents; the tier follows the facts of the return, never the other way around.

included: the written pre-work quote and its named exclusions
the stop-and-re-quote trigger and recorded approval
the concession authority and its limits
the rule that facts drive the tier and not the reverse
excluded: how the newly discovered work is technically performed, owned by the return workflow knowledge base
renegotiating fees with the returning base between seasons, owned by the returning-client knowledge base
any suggestion that a client may choose a lower tier by leaving facts out

pros.claim: Stopping at the trigger and re-quoting is the only mechanism that prevents complex returns from being delivered at simple-return prices year after year
pros.example: a second-state filing discovered in preparation, paused for approval rather than quietly absorbed

cons.claim: A mid-return repricing conversation lands at the worst possible moment for the relationship, and some clients will experience it as a change of terms however carefully it is framed
cons.example: a client of many years re-quoted in early April who takes the increase personally and does not return

failure_modes: absorbing scope changes silently to avoid an uncomfortable conversation
